statement: Let n=len(s). For 0<=i<n define c(i)=|ascii(s[i])-ascii(t[i])|, and for 0<=a<=b<=n define C(a,b)=sum_{i=a}^{b-1} c(i), with C(a,a)=0. The function returns a result r such that r is the greatest integer k with 0<=k<=n for which there exists an integer a with 0<=a<=n-k and C(a,a+k)<=maxCost. Equivalently, r is the maximum length of a contiguous substring of s whose total cost to become the corresponding substring of t is at most maxCost; if no positive length is affordable, r=0 (the empty substring has cost 0).
preconditions: len(t)=len(s); 1<=len(s)<=10^5; 0<=maxCost<=10^6; every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122).

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail (no overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic).
preconditions: len(t)=len(s); 1<=len(s)<=10^5; 0<=maxCost<=10^6; every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r <= len(s).
preconditions: len(t)=len(s); 1<=len(s)<=10^5; 0<=maxCost<=10^6; every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122).

statement: Let n=len(s). The returned value r equals the length of the longest contiguous block of indices i for which s[i]=t[i]; explicitly, r is the greatest integer k with 0<=k<=n such that there exists an integer a with 0<=a<=n-k and s[i]=t[i] for every i satisfying a<=i<a+k.
preconditions: len(t)=len(s); 1<=len(s)<=10^5; maxCost=0; every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122).
len(t)=len(s); 1<=len(s)<=10^5; 0<=maxCost<=10^6; every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122); for every i with 0<=i<len(s), s[i]=t[i].

statement: The function returns a result r, and r=0 if and only if for every i with 0<=i<len(s), |ascii(s[i])-ascii(t[i])| > maxCost.
preconditions: len(t)=len(s); 1<=len(s)<=10^5; 0<=maxCost<=10^6; every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122).

statement: Let n=len(s) and let C = sum_{i=0}^{n-1} |ascii(s[i])-ascii(t[i])|. The function returns a result r, and r=n if and only if C <= maxCost.
preconditions: len(t)=len(s); 1<=len(s)<=10^5; 0<=maxCost<=10^6; every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122).

statement: Let c = |ascii(s[0])-ascii(t[0])|. The function returns r=1 if c<=maxCost, and returns r=0 otherwise.
preconditions: len(t)=len(s); len(s)=1; 0<=maxCost<=10^6; every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r>0, there exists an integer a such that 0<=a<=len(s)-r and sum_{i=a}^{a+r-1} |ascii(s[i])-ascii(t[i])| <= maxCost.
preconditions: len(t)=len(s); 1<=len(s)<=10^5; 0<=maxCost<=10^6; every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer k with r<k<=len(s) and every integer a with 0<=a<=len(s)-k, we have sum_{i=a}^{a+k-1} |ascii(s[i])-ascii(t[i])| > maxCost.
preconditions: len(t)=len(s); 1<=len(s)<=10^5; 0<=maxCost<=10^6; every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122).

statement: For any valid inputs s,t,maxCost, let r be the result returned by equal_substring(s,t,maxCost) and let r' be the result returned by equal_substring(t,s,maxCost). Both calls return results and r=r'.
preconditions: len(t)=len(s); 1<=len(s)<=10^5; 0<=maxCost<=10^6; every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122).

statement: Let r1 be the result returned by equal_substring(s,t,m1) and let r2 be the result returned by equal_substring(s,t,m2). Both calls return results and r1<=r2.
preconditions: len(t)=len(s); 1<=len(s)<=10^5; every byte of s and t is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122); 0<=m1<=m2<=10^6.
